standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a disjoint union as a product
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma that the cohomology of a disjoint union is the product of the cohomologies, with the isomorphism given by the pullbacks along the coprojections
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the target of the degree map with the direct sum of the targets of the two degree maps.

standard_prerequisites.name: Decomposition of a class along the coprojections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The identity expressing a class on a disjoint union as the sum of the pushforwards of its pullbacks, established in the proof of the additivity lemma
standard_prerequisites.use: Splits the computation of the degree into the two summands.

core_obligations: Reduce to an identity (proof lines 3411-3421): the pullbacks along the two coprojections identify the cohomology of the disjoint union with the product, so the assertion means that under this identification the sum of the two degree maps corresponds to the degree map of the disjoint union.

Compute (proof lines 3421-3429): decomposing a class along the coprojections and applying the degree map gives the sum of the degrees of the two pulled back classes, which is exactly the asserted identity.
proof_roadmap: Use the isomorphism given by the coprojections to set up the identity.
Decompose a class and compute the degree to conclude.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the additivity of the degree map with respect to disjoint unions of nonempty equidimensional smooth projective schemes of the same dimension (statement lines 3407-3411). The proof (proof lines 3412-3429) uses the isomorphism expressing the cohomology of a disjoint union as a product and the decomposition of a class along the coprojections. H2: a complete short computation.
